newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Turk minister says March 98 may be best for vote.
newsitem.headline: Turk minister says March 98 may be best for vote.

text.p: A senior Turkish official said on Monday it might be best for early elections to be held in March 1998 but it was up to parliament to decide.
Ayfer Yilmaz, Turkish state minister for Foreign Economic Affairs, spoke while accompanying President Suleyman Demirel on a visit to the Baltic republic of Lithuania.

Demirel declined to answer questions on the political crisis in Turkey, sparked when its first Islamist prime minister Necmettin Erbakan said he would stand down and let conservative True Path Party leader Tansu Ciller lead the country until early elections. A date for the vote was not given.
But Yilmaz, a True Path member, said March may be the best time for the elections.
"We have to make first of all some changes in the election law. First of all we are thinking of it (the election) to be late autumn or December," she told Reuters.
"But what we can foresee is that March 1998 will be the best time maybe," she said.
She noted that an election in late 1997 would be in the winter, which would make it difficult for people to vote.
Yilmaz said that it was up to parliament to decide on the election date. "...We can't decide ... the date, but the parliament has to vote for the early election from now on."
In Ankara, True Path deputy chairman Hasan Ekinci said the election would take place by the end of the year.
"This election will be carried out by the end of 1997," Ekinci told a news conference.
